recommendation: Adopt a two-stage national prioritisation process
action: Use Opportunity Potential as a screening layer, then require cricket-specific readiness evidence before investment decisions.
rationale: Avoids treating demographic opportunity as actual demand and aligns investment with delivery capacity.

recommendation: Create a national Community Cricket Opportunity & Readiness dataset
action: Join PlayHQ/registration history, club/program locations, facility access, participant age/gender, and demographic growth at LGA/SA2 or club-catchment level.
rationale: Directly closes the largest limitation identified in this public-data prototype.

recommendation: Prioritise growth corridors, not only individual LGAs
action: Create corridor views for Melbourne outer growth belt, western/south-west Sydney, South East Queensland and Perth growth belt.
rationale: Phase 11 found 94.6% of Top-20 absolute junior growth concentrated in four broad urban growth systems.

recommendation: Build an annual junior-growth early-warning dashboard
action: Track target-age population growth, registrations, programs and facility capacity to flag areas where demographic growth is outpacing cricket supply.
rationale: Makes the model operational rather than a one-off report.

recommendation: Separate acquisition, capacity and retention KPIs
action: Do not judge every LGA on total registrations alone; distinguish new-player acquisition, returning players, transition/conversion and capacity constraints.
rationale: The job description explicitly separates acquisition, retention and churn modelling.

recommendation: Overlay women/girls and multicultural strategic priorities
action: Add direct registration and demographic layers for girls and culturally diverse communities rather than using broad demographic counts as demand assumptions.
rationale: CA has explicit women/girls and multicultural participation priorities.
